correctness.rationale: Equiangularity makes all vertex tangent cones have aperture pi-2pi/n and makes their inward bisectors equally spaced by 2pi/n. Thus any direction belongs to at most floor((n-1)/2) vertex illumination arcs. Summing the fractional vertex constraints gives the sharp lower bound. A cyclic family of maximal consecutive blocks supplies an explicit finite-support measure attaining it, and a convex-combination argument shows that satisfying the vertex constraints also satisfies every edge-interior constraint. Equality in the same double-counting chain yields the rigidity statement.
risks: The finite checker is diagnostic only; the universal statement rests on the exact arc-spacing argument.

value.rationale: The regular pentagon is the explicit nontrivial polygonal example singled out in the paper introducing fractional illumination. Closing that bound and extending it to every equiangular n-gon gives a complete natural class rather than an arbitrary slice. The theorem provides exact parity-dependent values, an explicit optimal finite measure, equality rigidity, and a clean normal-fan interpretation, with both branches converging to the smooth planar value 2.
risks: The theorem does not determine fractional illumination for arbitrary nonequiangular polygons.
